payload.body: Spectral-median (median frequency) is the full-spectrum energy-quantile summary that reports the frequency f_med at which half of the total spectral energy lies below and half above. Parameters: (1) the per-bin energy vector E = {E_i} over the full analyzed spectrum [f0, f_max), (2) the energy-weighted cumulative distribution C(f) = (sum of E_i for bins at frequency <= f) / (sum of all E_i), (3) the target quantile q, which the median fixes at q = 0.5; the reported value is the smallest frequency f such that C(f) >= q. It is a member of the same quantile family as spectral-rolloff, which fixes q at the 85% energy level: the median is the 50% level of that family and does not depend on a chosen high-level contour. It reads the full per-bin energy vector and carries no [f_low, f_high) band bounds, so it is a full-side summary rather than a band-local one. Persists as a standard energy-quantile summary in audio analysis, computed on the per-bin energy vector in MIR toolkits and reported in sound-description documentation. [formal: mediana spectri | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Cepstral-mean-variance normalization (CMVN) is a signal processing technique that normalizes cepstral coefficient vectors by computing the mean and variance across an utterance (or a sliding window) and applying z-score normalization to each frame. Parameters: (1) the mean is computed per coefficient dimension across all frames, (2) the variance is computed per coefficient dimension across all frames, (3) the normalization is applied element-wise as (c_i - μ_i) / σ_i for each coefficient c_i, where σ_i is the standard deviation. The technique removes both channel-induced mean shifts and variance mismatches between speakers. Persistence mechanism: implemented as a standard preprocessing step in speech recognition pipelines (Kaldi, HTK) and encoded in audio processing libraries (Python, MATLAB). payload.body: Jitter (period perturbation) is a voice-quality parameter quantifying the cycle-to-cycle variation of the fundamental period in a voiced speech signal. For N consecutive glottal cycles with periods P_i, the perturbation is computed as APQ1 = (1/(N-1)) * Σ_i |P_{i+1} - P_i| / ((1/N) * Σ_i P_i), or equivalently the standard deviation of the periods divided by their mean, reported in percent or in absolute units (milliseconds or seconds). Parameters: (1) the voiced speech signal segmented at pitch-synchronous cycle boundaries, (2) the per-cycle period measure, (3) the perturbation variant (APQ1 — average absolute difference, JRR — ratio, JDP — absolute difference). Small jitter indicates period stability (normal phonation); large jitter indicates period instability (dysphonia). Persistence mechanism: the standardized clinical voice-quality parameter computed by acoustic analysis software (Praat, laryngology toolkits) from pitch-synchronous period tracks; it persists as a documented measurement in voice-disorder assessment. [formal: titubatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.body: Electroglottography (EGG) is a non-invasive technique that measures glottal vocal-fold contact over time by passing a small alternating current through the vocal folds and recording the voltage across them. Because the glottal contact area modulates the electrical impedance of the vocal folds — high impedance when the glottis is open (air gap), low impedance when the folds are in contact — the peak-to-peak amplitude of the voltage is inversely related to glottal contact area, and its demodulated envelope, the electroglottogram (EGG waveform), tracks the open/close cycle of the glottis. Parameters: (1) excitation current — a small AC current kept below the safety threshold (typically ~0.5 mA peak at ~2.5 kHz); (2) electrode placement — two submental/neck electrodes completing the current path through the larynx; (3) demodulation — per-cycle peak-to-peak voltage measurement producing a continuous signal; (4) output — the electroglottogram, a time series whose amplitude is inversely proportional to glottal contact area. Persistence mechanism: standardized EGG transducers and laryngeal analysis systems (Kay PENTAGRAM, the laryngograph), documented in clinical laryngology and voice-disorder assessment; the waveform persists as a measured time series of glottal contact. Because the glottal contact area modulates the electrical impedance of the vocal folds — high impedance when the glottis is open (air gap), low impedance when the folds are in contact — the peak-to-peak amplitude of the voltage is inversely related to glottal contact area, and its demodulated envelope, the electroglottogram (EGG waveform), tracks the open/close cycle of the glottis. Parameters: (1) excitation current — a small AC current kept below the safety threshold (typically ~0.5 mA peak at ~2.5 kHz); (2) electrode placement — two submental/neck electrodes completing the current path through the larynx; (3) demodulation — per-cycle peak-to-peak voltage measurement producing a continuous signal; (4) output — the electroglottogram, a time series whose amplitude is inversely proportional to glottal contact area. Persistence mechanism: standardized EGG transducers and laryngeal analysis systems (Kay PENTAGRAM, the laryngograph), documented in clinical laryngology and voice-disorder assessment; the waveform persists as a measured time series of glottal contact. [formal: electroglottographia | substrate: matter | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.body: Voice-quality is a human-made family of standardized clinical parameters for assessing laryngeal function: a fixed, named set maintained as the measurement map of voice-disorder assessment. The family comprises period perturbation (jitter: APQ1, JRR, JDP), amplitude perturbation (shimmer: APQ3, standard-deviation variant), and source-contact measures derived from electroglottography (contact quotient, open quotient), each with a defined computation from the acoustic or electroglottographic signal, a standardized reporting unit (percent, dB, or quotient), and maintained reference ranges separating typical from disordered phonation. Parameters: (1) the parameter set and its named variants, (2) the computation — per-cycle measures over pitch-synchronous segments aggregated by the standard formulas, (3) the reference ranges and diagnostic thresholds the discipline maintains. Persistence mechanism: maintained by the discipline of laryngology and speech science — standardized in clinical practice, implemented in voice-analysis toolkits (Praat and laryngology suites), taught in voice-disorder curricula, and revised as the standard; the family persists as a maintained map of the natural territory of vocal health. The delta filter differentiates coefficient sequences: delta_d(t) = sum of n*c_d(t+n) over a symmetric window, where c_d is the coefficient value for dimension d - and the coefficients are samples of the cepstrum. Remove the cepstrum and there are no c_d values to differentiate, so the delta computation halts. The cepstrum is the parent representation of the operand, not a sibling restriction, so the band-distribution STRIKE line does not apply.

The SERVES claim rests on two weak links. First: the note argues that because speech-processing includes 'analysis' and EGG helps with 'voice-quality assessment,' EGG must serve speech-processing. This is overbroad — any measurement tool could be said to serve any analysis system that might use it. Second: standard speech-processing toolkits (Kaldi, HTK, librosa) operate on audio signals (MFCCs, pitch, formants), not on EGG glottal-contact waveforms. EGG's primary beneficiary is clinical laryngology and voice-disorder assessment, not speech-processing systems. The shimmer precedent cited (ge46f8f) is a voice perturbation measure computed from audio directly — a closer fit to speech-processing pipelines. EGG requires a dedicated transducer and is not part of standard speech-processing.

Law 9: HNR is a specific named member of the voice-quality family. The accepted voice-quality definition carves the family as 'a fixed, named set maintained as the measurement map of voice-disorder assessment' whose members each have 'a defined computation from the acoustic or electroglottographic signal, a standardized reporting unit (percent, dB, or quotient), and maintained reference ranges.' The accepted HNR definition satisfies every carved member condition: a defined computation (10·log10 of harmonic energy over aperiodic residual energy from a short-time spectrum), a standardized unit (dB), maintained reference ranges, persisting 'as a standardized descriptor in speech pathology, voice quality assessment' implemented in the same laryngology toolkits (Praat, VoiceSauce) the family definition names. HNR is the standard third member alongside jitter and shimmer — the classic jitter/shimmer/HNR triad of voice-disorder assessment. Nearest accepted kind for a standardized parameter of voice-disorder assessment is this family, not a generic spectral feature. INSTANCE_OF to the nearest kind, same class as the accepted jitter and shimmer members.

Persisted through textbook treatment in DSP (Rabiner and Schafer), implementation in speech analysis toolkits (Praat, MATLAB, Kaldi), and standard use in source-filter separation.

payload.body: Inverse-filtering is a signal processing technique that estimates and removes the effect of a known or estimated system transfer function from a signal, effectively recovering the original input that passed through that system. The method operates by: (1) obtaining the estimated transfer function H(z) of the system to be inverted (e.g., the linear-prediction filter for the vocal tract), (2) constructing the inverse filter H_inv(z) = 1/H(z), (3) filtering the observed signal with H_inv(z) to produce the residual or excitation signal. Parameters: (1) the transfer function to invert — typically a finite-order all-pole model estimated from the signal itself, (2) the input signal — the observed output of the system, (3) the inversion method — direct division in the z-domain, iterative regularization, or frequency-domain division. The persistence mechanism is algorithmic implementation: the inverse filter is encoded in DSP software (e.g., Praat, MATLAB, Kaldi), documented in signal processing textbooks, and standardized in speech analysis toolkits for source-filter separation. [formal: filtrum inversum | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Open quotient (OQ) is a voice-quality parameter quantifying the fraction of the fundamental period during which the glottis is open in voiced phonation. From the frame-aligned glottal-flow waveform g(n) (glottogram) and the fundamental period T0, the open phase is the interval between the flow maximum (Fmax) and the flow minimum (Fmin) — or between the zero crossings of the flow derivative — and OQ = open phase / T0. Parameters: (1) the glottal-flow waveform estimated per voiced frame, (2) the fundamental period T0 from pitch tracking, (3) the open-phase extraction method (Fmax–Fmin difference or flow-derivative zero crossings). It is reported as a dimensionless ratio; the maintained reference range for typical phonation sits near 0.5–0.7, and a reduced open quotient indicates excessive glottal closure. Persistence mechanism: the standardized clinical voice-quality parameter computed by voice-analysis software (Praat, laryngology suites) from the glottogram, taught in voice-disorder curricula, and revised as the standard; it persists as a maintained member of the voice-quality measurement map. [formal: quota apertae | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]
